trial.title: Study of Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of GB221 in Infants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 1

endpoints.measure: Number of participants with treatment-related adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) at Grade 3 or higher as characterized by CTCAEv5.0
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assess the number of treatment-related AEs and SAEs as characterized by CTCAEv5.0

endpoints.measure: Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Changes in Physical Functions
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assess the number of participants with clinically significant changes in physical functions.

endpoints.measure: Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Changes in Neurological Functions
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assess the number of participants with clinically significant changes in neurological functions.

endpoints.measure: Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Changes in Vital signs
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assess the number of participants with clinically significant changes in vital signs.

endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: ECG will measure RR interval, P Wave, PR interval, PR segment, QRS Complex, ST segment, T wave and QT Interval.

endpoints.measure: Change in serum cardiac troponin I levels
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits

endpoints.measure: Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Laboratory Abnormalities as Measured Using Hematology, Chemistry and Coagulation Tests
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assess the number of participants with clinically significant laboratory changes including hematology, serum chemistry, and coagulation tests.

endpoints.measure: Number of Participants with Clinically Significant Laboratory Abnormalities as Measured Using Urine and CSF Tests
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assess the number of participants with clinically significant laboratory changes including urine and CSF tests.

endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits
endpoints.description: Assessment of humoral (NAb and TAb titers) and T-cell (IFNγ ELISpot) immune responses to the AAVhu68 capsid and SMN transgene product in serum and CSF.

endpoints.measure: Assess the number of participants who experience permanent ventilation or death
endpoints.time_frame: Up to 18 months across multiple visits

endpoints.measure: Percentage of infants with improvement in the motor milestones categories in Section 2 of the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE), with the exclusion of voluntary grasp.
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline, 6 months and 18 months post dose.
endpoints.description:
* improvement in at least one category, i.e., an increase in the score for head control, rolling, sitting, crawling, standing, or walking of ≥1 point,
* an increase in the score for kicking of ≥2 points, or achievement of the maximal score for kicking.

endpoints.measure: Change from baseline in mean Children's Hospital of Philadelphia Infant Test of Neuromuscular Disorders (CHOP-INTEND) Score.
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline, 6 months and 18 months post dose.
endpoints.description: Assess 16 types of muscle movements, each given a score from zero (the person can't complete the movement) to 4 (the person can complete the movement on their own, without assistance) to produce a score of 0 to 64.

outcome.rationale: Phase 1/2 first-in-human trial with no clinical data. Safety profile expected similar to other AAV gene therapies (manageable with immunosuppression). Efficacy likely but magnitude uncertain due to novel vector and delivery route. Success depends on demonstrating acceptable safety and preliminary efficacy signals to enable Phase 3.

analysis_trace: Trial Identification: NCT07070999 is the Phase 1/2 CHARISMA trial evaluating GB221, a next-generation AAVhu68-based gene therapy for SMA Type 1 delivered via intracisterna magna injection. First patient dosed February 2026 per press release (PRNewswire). Expected completion 2028.
Indication: Spinal muscular atrophy type 1 (SMA1), severe neurodegenerative disease caused by SMN1 mutations. Untreated patients typically do not survive beyond 18 months.

Patient Population: Two cohorts - symptomatic (2 weeks to <12 months, disease onset <6 months) and presymptomatic (2 weeks to <5 months, at risk). N=22 estimated. Includes treatment-naïve or risdiplam-treated participants.
Target Mechanism: AAVhu68 capsid delivering codon-optimized SMN1 transgene via ICM injection to motor neurons. Designed to reduce overexpression toxicities vs systemic delivery.

Evidence Sources: (1) PRNewswire Feb 2026 - first patient dosed, trial design; (2) PMC8075402 - onasemnogene safety in SMA (hepatotoxicity, thrombocytopenia, troponin elevation); (3) PMC9411526 - AAV immunogenicity mechanisms; (4) PMC12974193 - meta-analysis AAEs 30% overall, hepatotoxicity 23.8%, myocarditis 6.2%, TMA 4.7%; (5) PMC7002897 - ICM delivery safety in Tay-Sachs; (6) Company website - preclinical data showing survival benefit in mouse SMA model.

Evidence Role Assessment: No direct GB221 clinical outcome data available (trial just initiated). Using indirect evidence from approved AAV9-SMA gene therapy (onasemnogene) and other AAV gene therapies. Evidence_role: indirect_direction for safety endpoints; mechanism_background for efficacy. Mismatch: different vector (AAVhu68 vs AAV9), different delivery route (ICM vs IV), different patient population (younger infants in GB221).

Safety Analysis: AAV gene therapies show class effects - hepatotoxicity, cardiac troponin elevation, thrombocytopenia, immune responses. Meta-analysis shows ~30% immunotoxicity rate. GB221 uses modified expression cassette to reduce toxicity. ICM delivery may reduce systemic exposure vs IV. Prophylactic immunosuppression per protocol (prednisolone). Predict Grade 3+ AEs in 15-35% range.

Efficacy Analysis: No human efficacy data for GB221. Preclinical mouse model showed survival and neuromotor improvement. Approved gene therapy (onasemnogene) showed CHOP-INTEND improvements of 20-40 points and HINE milestone achievement in 80-100% of treated infants. Presymptomatic treatment yields better outcomes. Extrapolating to GB221: likely efficacy signal but magnitude uncertain due to vector and delivery differences.

Key Risks: (1) Immune-mediated AEs given AAV immunogenicity; (2) Unknown optimal dose for ICM delivery; (3) Young age of participants increases vulnerability; (4) First-in-human uncertainty; (5) Long-term durability unknown.
Coverage Gaps: No published GB221 clinical data; no ICM-delivered AAV gene therapy efficacy data in SMA; exact dosing not disclosed; immunogenicity rates specific to AAVhu68 unknown.
